title: Bolder hand: choose the visual world
question: You asked for bolder: six foreign forms, nothing safe. The first one dealt leads. Each sketch is the live run screen. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Graphite Seams
options.lineage: dark-first developer consoles, GitHub's own type family
options.thesis: A graphite workbench of persistent tiled panels where every step is coloured like syntax: verbs, paths and numbers read the way code does.
options.viewport: Thin top bar with the run's lifecycle strip; three tiled panels (step tree, live log, provenance) divided by hairline seams; Cancel run isolated alone at the far right.
options.risk: Dark dev consoles are a familiar genre; the syntax-coloured steps and lifecycle strip must carry the distinction.

raised.raise: Review takes over: one flag owns the whole work area at a time, and the next flag is one keypress away.
Every run carries the same fixed-scale lifecycle strip (Queued, Running, Recovering, Review, PR) so runs compare at a glance.

options.label: Boarding Pass
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and live gate boards
options.thesis: Each run is a ticket from issue to pull request; the org board reranks live and a changed run stays lit in signal orange until someone notices.
options.viewport: Left: dark live board of org runs in fixed columns. Right: the selected run as a segmented pass (FROM repo, TO pull request, ISSUE, MODEL, SEQ), its hash as the scannable block, status GATE HOLD.
options.case: The strongest demo-screenshot moment in the hand; the pass metaphor is a stretch for audit-log and settings screens.
options.risk: If the ticket grows decorative it becomes a costume; the segments must hold real run data.

options.label: Emission Rail
options.lineage: glass spectrograms on a light box
options.thesis: The whole run is one spectrum: every step a hairline on a charcoal rail; state is line form, so a rollback is a struck line and a security flag is a doubled sodium-yellow line.
options.viewport: A full-width spectrum rail of all 37 steps across the top (struck lines for rollbacks, a doubled yellow line for FLAG-3); below it, ash panels for the selected step, live log and provenance.
options.case: The most original wow moment, and state-by-shape is accessible; the rail is unfamiliar at first sight.
options.risk: Hairline encoding needs a legend early, or first-time viewers will not decode it.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.thesis: The run is a course: checkpoints are numbered controls, the agent's path rides in purple, and a rollback is a leg drawn back to an earlier control.
options.viewport: Top: the run as a course map (React Flow) with numbered checkpoint circles and purple legs, rollback legs dashed back; below: the control description table and live log.
options.case: Checkpoint graph is a great fit for React Flow and very memorable; it is a light page, which you said felt plain.
options.risk: Light ground again; the colour comes from the map inks, not the shell.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the screen; the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: One run per screen with action glyphs on the right.
options.case: Entertainment register and no media to fill it; loses both axes.
options.kept: Review: one flag owns the work area at a time.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject at identical scale through every stage.
options.viewport: Five plates of a run's life stages.
options.case: Cream editorial reads as the very slop you want to avoid; loses both axes.
options.kept: A fixed-scale lifecycle strip on every run.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer dashboard every AI dev tool ships, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark side nav, run list and live terminal panes, blue primary buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
